subject: Proposal: availability baseline and monthly remedy schedule for Nextrail
messages:
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@nextrail.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: contracts@nextrail.com, maria.gomez@procurely.io
Date: 2026-07-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: SLA template questions + monthly remedy cap

Kimberly —

Thanks for sending the initial SLA template. We reviewed the availability bands and the credit ladder. A couple of items that are blockers for procurement:

- Nextrail needs a clearer monthly credit cap rather than an open-ended percentage of spend. Can you propose a flat monthly cap or a formula tied to committed spend?
- The baseline uptime of 99.9% is acceptable for most services, but our operations team is asking whether you can offer 99.95% for the hosted inference endpoint used for realtime routing (priority tier). If that's not feasible, what additional remedies would you offer for sustained degradations?
- We also need the maintenance carveouts clearly defined (scheduled vs. emergency). The current template language is broad.

Attached is a short extract of an incident log (sample) so you can see typical patterns. Maria from procurement is copied to coordinate contract language.

Can we get a revised proposal by Tuesday? We are aiming to get legal sign-off the week after.

Sanjay
Director, Platform Engineering\Nextrail Systems

Attachments: downtime-log-sample.csv (excerpt)

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@nextrail.com>
Cc: contracts@nextrail.com, maria.gomez@procurely.io
Date: 2026-07-11T13:45:22-07:00
Subject: Re: SLA template questions + monthly remedy cap

Sanjay —

Thanks for the clear note and the sample log — that helped. High level response below; attaching a formal counterproposal in PDF.

Proposed changes (summary):

- Availability baseline: 99.9% standard across most routes; we can offer a 99.95% uptime commitment specifically for your "priority" hosted inference endpoint (single model endpoint) if you commit to a 12‑month reserved capacity pool and a minimum monthly spend (we propose $50k/mo).
- Monthly credit cap: propose a two‑tier cap: either 30% of the monthly committed invoice or a hard cap of $75k, whichever is lower. This keeps credits bounded while preserving meaningful remediation.
- Sustained degradation remedy: if a priority endpoint experiences >10 minutes of continuous degraded availability in a 24‑hour window beyond the SLO, we will (a) issue an automatic pro‑rata credit and (b) provide a one‑time operational credit geared toward a free incident review and a remediation playbook within 10 business days.
- Maintenance carveouts: scheduled maintenance will be announced 72 hours in advance and excluded up to 4 hours/month; anything beyond that will count toward availability. Emergency maintenance will be limited and justified with post‑incident notes; credits will apply if emergency maintenance exceeds a reasonable threshold.

I attached the PDF with exact contract language and the credit matrix for your review. If that aligns with procurement's constraints, we can prepare the DocuSign and route to legal. If not, let me know which line items to adjust and I'll loop in Sales Ops and Legal.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Sales, East
Redwood Inference

Attachments: nextrail-sla-draft-v2.pdf, redwood-credit-matrix.xlsx

Subject: Final counterproposal and next steps (Nextrail SLA)

Sanjay / Maria —

Thanks for the quick turn. We reviewed internally and have a final counterproposal attached. Summary of the main points: 

- Availability: 99.9% standard across the account; 99.95% for the named "priority" hosted inference endpoint subject to a 12‑month reserved capacity commitment at $50,000/mo minimum.
- Monthly remedy: credits are computed pro‑rata by the monthly invoice with a cap equal to the lesser of 30% of committed spend or $75,000.
- Sustained degradation: automatic pro‑rata credit for continuous degradation >10 minutes in any 24‑hour period; plus a single operational remediation credit (covers incident postmortem + playbook) per quarter if repeated degradations occur.
- Maintenance carveouts: scheduled maintenance announced >=72 hours is excluded up to 4 hours/month; emergency maintenance will be limited and documented with cause and mitigation plan — credits apply if emergency maintenance exceeds 6 hours in a calendar month.
- Latency SLO: we agreed to include a soft latency SLO (95th percentile < 120ms for priority endpoint) with monthly monitoring; latency shortfalls will trigger operations support but not monetary credits unless they coincide with availability degradations.

Next steps:
- Please review the attached PDF and the credit matrix. If this aligns, we will open a DocuSign envelope (link below) with the SLA amendment and reserved‑capacity addendum.
- If procurement needs a lower hard cap, we can consider a tiered reduction tied to the initial 6 months of usage with a review at month 6 — let me know.
